raw_response:
I been farming this land fifty years. My man passed, it's just me and my daughter-in-law now, but I still handle the cotton myself. Eight mu is what I got, all cotton, same as always. I don't change much year to year — what works, works.

For seeds, I buy the ones the dealer in town sells, the kind everyone plants now — the bug-resistant cotton. My neighbor Old Wang started with it years back, bollworm didn't eat his field up like before, so I switched too. I don't know the name, I just ask for the same packet as last year. About one jin of seed per mu, maybe a bit more to be safe.

For fertilizer — I put down two bags of the compound stuff, the 15-15-15 kind, before planting. That's one hundred jin per mu. Then when the cotton starts setting bolls, I go back with urea, maybe half a bag per mu, forty-fifty jin. I always put a little extra. If I put too little and the plants look yellow, I cry all season. A few extra yuan on fertilizer I can stand, but a bad harvest I cannot.

I plough the field proper in spring, not that lazy rotary business. My father ploughed deep, I plough deep.

Water — I pump from the well. Once before planting to wet the ground, then two, three more times when it's hot and the bolls are filling. Four times total, maybe.

Bugs are the worst part of cotton. Even with the new seed, the aphids still come, and the red spiders, and those little bugs that suck the leaves. I spray maybe seven, eight times through the season. My nephew helps carry the sprayer now, my shoulders don't work like before.

A good year I get two hundred fifty jin of lint per mu. Bad year maybe two hundred. I hope for good.
